video_title: Could Some Vaults Trigger Securities Law? Yes, but It's Case by Case
gist: Sun Ragupathi, co-founder/CEO of vault infrastructure provider Veta, argues that onchain vaults (~$67B TVL) have become DeFi's real distribution layer via fintechs like Kraken, Robin Hood, Coinbase and MetaMask, and that SEC Commissioner Hester Peirce's statement is a facts-and-circumstances signal rather than a warning shot: lending vaults over protocols like Morpho are not securities in his view, but vaults taking direct exposure to tokenized securities clearly implicate securities law. He claims smart-contract risk has collapsed over the last 5 years while operational/key-management risk is now where exploits concentrate, and says post-Stream Finance the industry has visibly scaled back yield-chasing — though he expects a Stream-style blowup to recur because open access to longtail collateral is a core DeFi value prop.

themes.theme: Vaults as DeFi's fintech distribution layer

insights.claim: Onchain vaults already represent roughly $67 billion in TVL, making them a major DeFi category rather than an emerging experiment.
insights.speaker: Laura Shin
insights.so_what: Sizes the addressable market for vault infrastructure, curation and rating businesses, and explains why regulators are now engaging with the category.
insights.quote: they're already a big business about $67 billion in TVL and vaults

insights.claim: Vaults are best understood as infrastructure for building financial products on top of onchain markets — spanning lending, RWA baskets and trading strategies — not as a single product type.
insights.speaker: Sun Ragupathi
insights.so_what: Investors should underwrite each vault by its underlying strategy and risk stack rather than treating 'vault' as a comparable asset class.
insights.quote: So vaults are basically onchain vehicles for giving users exposure to onchain markets, right?

insights.claim: Net new DeFi users are now arriving almost entirely through fintech platforms where they already hold stablecoins, rather than by creating wallets and using peer-to-peer protocols directly.
insights.speaker: Sun Ragupathi
insights.so_what: Value in DeFi is shifting toward whoever owns distribution and the packaging layer, not just the underlying protocol tokens.
insights.quote: most of the net new people who are actually getting exposure to these markets and protocols are coming through fintech platforms

insights.claim: The largest fintechs building vaults today — Robin Hood, Coinbase, Kraken and MetaMask — are overwhelmingly routing to onchain lending protocols such as Morpho, Kamino and Jupiter.
insights.speaker: Sun Ragupathi
insights.so_what: Lending protocols with fintech integrations are the direct beneficiaries of retail vault flows; watch their deposit growth as a proxy for fintech earn adoption.

insights.claim: Vault demand will migrate beyond simple lending toward tokenized treasuries, money market funds and baskets of tokenized equities as more assets move onchain.
insights.speaker: Sun Ragupathi
insights.so_what: Signals where the next vault product cycle goes, and where vaults start intersecting directly with securities regulation.

insights.claim: Vaults do not create new yield sources — they repackage existing onchain markets into a preference-based interface where users express risk tolerance and withdrawal needs instead of picking protocols.
insights.speaker: Sun Ragupathi
insights.so_what: Any vault yield premium over base protocol yield is compensation for added risk, not alpha — a useful screen when comparing fintech earn products.
insights.quote: I wouldn't characterize this as vaults are doing something fundamentally different from the onchain world. They're just packaging up the markets that many different parties have created on chain

insights.claim: Crypto degens functioned as unpaid beta testers who risked their own capital to battle-test onchain infrastructure that institutions are only now adopting.
insights.speaker: Sun Ragupathi
insights.so_what: Frames the 2021 yield-farming era as an R&D subsidy — an argument that today's institutional adoption rests on already-stress-tested primitives.
insights.quote: eun are kind of like the beta testers of the onchain world

insights.claim: A vault must solve three dimensions simultaneously — access to the widest set of chains/assets/strategies, control via compliance and risk guardrails, and verifiability of where assets sit and when they can be withdrawn.
insights.speaker: Sun Ragupathi
insights.so_what: A ready-made diligence checklist for comparing vault providers and for spotting products that optimize access while skimping on control or transparency.

insights.claim: Fintechs underwriting vault products require the ability to impose their own compliance policies and risk controls, which is why distribution is pulling vault design toward configurable guardrails.
insights.speaker: Sun Ragupathi
insights.so_what: Vault infrastructure that cannot express per-distributor compliance constraints will be locked out of the largest distribution channels.

insights.claim: Every vault deployment involves three distinct parties — the infrastructure provider holding and deploying assets in smart contracts, the curator doing risk management and collateral selection, and the distributor owning the user relationship.
insights.speaker: Sun Ragupathi
insights.so_what: Loss attribution and legal exposure differ by party, so investors and users should ask which of the three actually made the decision that produced a loss.
insights.quote: There's the vault infrastructure provider that's creating that platform and the smart contracts that actually hold and deploy the assets. There's the curator that's doing the risk management

insights.claim: Onchain transparency is positioned as the structural fix for the FTX/BlockFi failure mode where centralized intermediaries took unaccountable risk with customer assets invisibly.
insights.speaker: Sun Ragupathi
insights.so_what: The pitch for vaults over CeFi yield products rests on verifiability — if a vault obscures asset location, it forfeits its main differentiator versus 2022-era lenders.
insights.quote: you don't get the like FTX, BlockFi issue where um there's centralized intermediaries who are taking uh basically unaccountable risk with your assets and you have no idea what's going on

themes.theme: Risk stack: smart contract to operational to economic

insights.claim: Vault losses arise from three stacked layers — smart contract risk, operational/key-management risk, and economic/collateral risk — and different parties secure different layers.
insights.speaker: Sun Ragupathi
insights.so_what: Gives a structured way to decompose any vault blowup post-mortem and to price which layer a given product is most exposed to.
insights.quote: It goes from smart contract to operational to economic risk.

insights.claim: Smart contract risk has fallen sharply over the last six to twelve months thanks to better coding practices and auditing tools, so very few exploits at scale now stem from contract bugs.
insights.speaker: Sun Ragupathi
insights.so_what: Audit count is a weakening differentiator between vault providers; diligence budgets should shift to operations.
insights.quote: smart contract risk has come way down as we've converged on much better coding practices, better auditing tools, better cyber, you know, capabilities

insights.claim: Risk has migrated to the governance and key-management layer — protocol upgrade rights and market whitelisting — and most major exploits of the last six months, including the Kelp and Drift incidents, were operational failures rather than code flaws.
insights.speaker: Sun Ragupathi
insights.so_what: Screen vaults and their dependencies for who holds upgrade and whitelist keys; that is now the dominant tail risk, and it is not covered by an audit report.
insights.quote: Basically many of the major exploits that we've seen over the last six months were operational failures.

insights.claim: Even a plain lending strategy carries the economic risk that collateral value collapses faster than it can be liquidated, for example when the collateral asset itself is exploited and instantly loses all value.
insights.speaker: Sun Ragupathi
insights.so_what: Liquidation speed versus collateral volatility is the key parameter for 'safe' lending vaults, especially those accepting longtail or wrapped assets.

insights.claim: Vault insurance programs are launching but none has yet processed a major claim, so their protection value is unproven.
insights.speaker: Sun Ragupathi
insights.so_what: Do not discount vault risk for advertised insurance until a claim event demonstrates payout behavior; the first major claim will be a repricing event for the category.
insights.quote: We haven't seen a major claim be processed yet. So that's always something that people should be skeptical of.

insights.claim: When a vault loses money the user does not always eat it — distributors, underlying protocols or the vault provider may absorb losses for commercial and reputational reasons, alongside formal insurance transfer.
insights.speaker: Sun Ragupathi
insights.so_what: Balance-sheet backstops from large-brand distributors are an unpriced, discretionary put; conversely, small distributors offer no such cushion.

insights.claim: End users cannot realistically audit the key-management supply chain themselves, so the industry needs operational standards plus third-party ratings — a category forming with crypto-native players like Credora within Redstone and traditional agencies such as S&P now interested in rating vaults.
insights.speaker: Sun Ragupathi
insights.so_what: Vault ratings are an emerging profit pool and a likely gating requirement for institutional allocation; watch S&P's entry as the legitimizing signal.
insights.quote: We can't expect end users to be able to do the diligence to look at the supply chain and see which keys have which roles. It's just not practical.

insights.claim: Baseline key-management best practice for vault partners is multisigs with time locks where every signer uses hardware keys, and avoiding blind signing on non-isolated devices.
insights.speaker: Sun Ragupathi
insights.so_what: A concrete diligence question set for any counterparty in a vault stack; absence of time locks is a red flag given operational risk now dominates.
insights.quote: important keys should be secured by multi-igs with time locks um where every signer is using hardware keys

insights.claim: The November Stream Finance blowup created roughly $285 million of exposure in vaults, concentrated in vaults whose curators had chased high yields.
insights.speaker: Laura Shin
insights.so_what: Establishes the loss magnitude that reset curator behavior, and a benchmark for sizing future curator-driven contagion.
insights.quote: an incident last November with Stream Finance. It blew up and created about $285 million worth of exposure in vaults

insights.claim: Risk-taking onchain has visibly scaled back since the Stream Finance events, driven by users pulling funds broadly and curators becoming more conscientious.
insights.speaker: Sun Ragupathi
insights.so_what: Implies current vault yields are lower but better-collateralized — a spread compression to expect and a signal that curator competition has shifted to safety.
insights.quote: there has absolutely been a scaling back of risk-taking on chain

insights.claim: The structural driver of vault blowups is that curators competing on headline yield must keep moving down the risk curve, often without users understanding the added risk.
insights.speaker: Sun Ragupathi
insights.so_what: Treat a persistent top-of-leaderboard yield as evidence of undisclosed risk rather than curator skill.
insights.quote: the only way to juice yields on these products is to continue going farther down the risk curve

insights.claim: A Stream-style vault blowup will happen again because financing against complex longtail assets is a core DeFi value proposition, so residual risk is a design feature rather than a bug to eliminate.
insights.speaker: Sun Ragupathi
insights.so_what: Position sizing across vaults should assume recurring idiosyncratic losses; the investable question is disclosure quality, not risk elimination.
insights.quote: Now, do I think that this will never happen again? I don't think so. I think it will happen at some point in the future.

insights.claim: The critical failure in vault products is mislabeling, not risk itself: users must not be sold something that feels like an insured savings account while actually giving exposure to what amounts to an onchain hedge fund.
insights.speaker: Sun Ragupathi
insights.so_what: Disclosure quality — not headline APY — is the variable regulators and users will judge, and the likely locus of the next enforcement or reputational hit.
insights.quote: they shouldn't think they're having some safe, you know, insured savings account and suddenly they're getting exposure to basically an onchain hedge fund like stream finance

insights.claim: Curator evaluation should start with operating history, track record and size, then test for dual competence in traditional collateral underwriting and DeFi-specific technical and governance risk.
insights.speaker: Sun Ragupathi
insights.so_what: A screen that would have flagged yield-chasing newer curators before Stream; favors incumbency and penalizes curators strong on only one of the two skill sets.

themes.theme: Securities law: Peirce statement and Howey

insights.claim: SEC Commissioner Hester Peirce stated a vault could be a common enterprise in which users invest money expecting profits from the deployers' and curators' entrepreneurial or managerial efforts — language drawn directly from the Howey test.
insights.speaker: Laura Shin
insights.so_what: Confirms the SEC is applying Howey to vault structures, making curator discretion a key legal risk factor to price into vault business models.
insights.quote: A vault, for example, could be a common enterprise in which users invest money with a reasonable expectation of profits to be derived from the vault deployers and curators entrepreneurial or managerial efforts.

insights.claim: Regulatory attention on vaults arrived now precisely because the products finally reached mainstream distribution — Robin Hood's earn launch put DeFi exposure in front of users who have never touched DeFi.
insights.speaker: Sun Ragupathi
insights.so_what: Regulatory scrutiny should be read as a success indicator for the category rather than an existential threat, but it also front-runs further fintech launches.
insights.quote: it was inevitable that this would get the attention of regulators precisely because these products are finally becoming successful

insights.claim: Whether a vault implicates securities law is a case-by-case function of its design, and the industry error is treating twenty structurally different products as one regulatory category.
insights.speaker: Sun Ragupathi
insights.so_what: Legal risk is not uniform across vault providers; underwriting must be per-vault, which favors providers that can document design distinctions.
insights.quote: you can't just call 20 different things a vault and pretend that they're all the same thing and carry the same risks and the same regulatory implications

insights.claim: Veta's position is that DeFi protocols and markets like Aave and Morpho are not securities, so vaults doing pure onchain lending do not take exposure to underlying securities — while vaults holding tokenized securities clearly do implicate securities law.
insights.speaker: Sun Ragupathi
insights.so_what: Draws the likely regulatory fault line: lending vaults versus tokenized-equity/treasury vaults, which will need different legal wrappers and may carry different distribution economics.
insights.quote: our view at VA is that you know D5 protocols and markets like A and Morpho are not securities

insights.claim: The binding constraint on institutional vault adoption is legal ambiguity, not technology — many financial institutions are dipping their toes in and would scale up given clear guidelines.
insights.speaker: Sun Ragupathi
insights.so_what: Regulatory clarity is the catalyst to watch for a step-change in vault TVL; the Peirce statement is arguably bullish rather than bearish for the sector.
insights.quote: what's preventing them from jumping all the way in is a lack of clarity and uh guidelines for what what these products are and what the laws are that surround them

insights.claim: Veta's Kraken DeFi earn partnership, launched in January with three stablecoin products and later extended to BTC earn, has grown to over $600 million in assets across more than 80,000 users, many with no prior DeFi experience.
insights.speaker: Sun Ragupathi
insights.so_what: A concrete conversion benchmark (~$7.5k average per user) for exchange-distributed DeFi earn products, useful for sizing Coinbase and Robin Hood equivalents.
insights.quote: we've grown to over 600 million in assets across over 80,000 users, many of whom may have never used DeFi before

insights.claim: The Kraken result is presented as proof that enterprise distribution — embedding packaged onchain markets inside platforms that already have millions of users — is the winning export path for DeFi.
insights.speaker: Sun Ragupathi
insights.so_what: Favors DeFi protocols and infra providers with signed enterprise channels over those relying on direct-to-degen acquisition.
insights.quote: Kraken has I think confirmed beyond any sort of doubt that enterprise distribution is the right way to export DeFi to the world

insights.claim: The vault stack is layered rather than winner-take-all: Centura curates the Kraken products Veta powers, Morpho runs its own vault protocol while Veta is one of Morpho's largest users, so nominal competitors are also counterparties.
insights.speaker: Sun Ragupathi
insights.so_what: Competitive mapping in vaults must be done layer by layer; headline 'competitor' lists overstate rivalry and understate mutual dependency risk.

insights.claim: Cooperation dominates competition in vaults today because the category is early enough that growing the pie beats fighting for share.
insights.speaker: Sun Ragupathi
insights.so_what: Expect partnership-driven growth and cross-integration rather than margin-destroying price wars in the near term — a reason vault infra margins may hold.
insights.quote: it just doesn't make sense to be knives out in a category that still has a thousandx to go from here

insights.claim: Veta's claimed moat is maturity rather than features: five years building vaults, tested at billion-dollar enterprise scale, with no security incident, in a market where enterprises refuse to be the first integration.
insights.speaker: Sun Ragupathi
insights.so_what: If enterprise buyers really do buy precedent, incumbency compounds and late-entering vault infra providers face a structural distribution disadvantage.
insights.quote: Nobody wants to be the first one to integrate some net new piece of infrastructure and take additional risk in what's already a fairly risky offering.
